notes: Actual general-fund results for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2025, as reported to the MA Division of Local Services on Schedule A, not a budget.

Includes public schools. Massachusetts cities and towns pay for their schools, and their share of any regional school district, from the general fund, where many other states have separate school districts, so spending and property tax per resident run higher than in those states. Schools are left out of the services and overhead shares.
Intergovernmental assessments are state and county charges deducted from state aid, mostly charter school tuition and school choice, plus transit and county charges. They are counted with schools.

Fixed costs ($110,800: health insurance, pensions and other benefits, including for school staff) are spread across departments, including schools, in proportion to their size. Debt service is left out of that spread.

Property tax is the certified tax levy ($1,714,841). The rest of the taxes on Schedule A ($455,173) is shown as other taxes and excises: motor vehicle excise, local-option meals and room excises, and penalties and interest. Taxes collected in a year can differ slightly from the levy, so this split is close but not exact.
Covers the general fund. Water, sewer and other enterprise funds, and regional school districts and other separate authorities, are not included.

Political money is not scored: candidates for office here file campaign reports with the city or town clerk, not the state. Only candidates for mayor, and for city council in some cities, file itemized reports with the MA Office of Campaign and Political Finance.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-15. A government with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

Transparency: Town of Washington has filed its Schedule A annual financial report with the Division of Local Services for FY 2025, the latest year most MA governments have filed. This is a check that the report was filed, not an opinion on its contents. The other five practices have not been checked yet, so they are left out of the score.
